input.question: What's keeping us from teaching animals to speak in human languages
input.ground_truth: The "hardware" (we talk the way we do because of the physiology of our tongues, teeth, palates, and vocal cords, other animals do not have this same setup) and the "software" (human brains have different "communication centers" than other animals).

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What's keeping us from teaching animals to speak in human languages

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your dog want to talk to each other. You know how to talk with words, but your dog barks and wags their tail. Dogs and other animals have their own ways to talk to each other, like barking, meowing, or making sounds we can’t always understand.

Our brains are really different from animal brains. We learn to talk by listening and practicing a lot when we’re little. Animals don’t have the same kind of voice or brain parts that help us make and understand human words. So, even if we try really hard, animals can’t learn to talk like us because their bodies and brains work differently.

It’s a bit like trying to teach a fish to ride a bike. Fish live in water and don’t have legs, so it’s really hard for them to ride a bike, even if they wanted to!
